extracted.intended_audience: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 Technical Papers reviewers (paper reviewers for SIGGRAPH Asia)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and ethical rules for reviewing Technical Papers submitted to SIGGRAPH Asia 2026, covering evaluation criteria for Journal vs Conference tracks, review content and tone, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, comparisons to prior work, and procedural requirements (formats, deadlines, online system).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal vs Conference track criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal Papers are expected to satisfy the ACM TOG criteria of excellence, and present original, well-validated, and comprehensively described research advancing computer graphics and interactive techniques. Conference Papers are expected to present original research advancing computer graphics and interactive techniques, but the evidence supporting these advances might not be as comprehensive as expected for Journal Papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review dual-track and journal-only submissions on a single scale. First decide if the paper's overall contribution merits acceptance to the Technical Papers program; if so, evaluate completeness and comprehensiveness to choose Journal vs Conference. Conference track should be open to less polished but novel ideas; journal requires a superset of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspiration and impact (follow-on research)
rubrics_metrics.description: An important factor in evaluating a paper is the degree to which it will inspire follow-on research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be fair and promote a broad range of substantial contributions; weigh potential to 'propel the field forward' against academic grounding to maintain SIGGRAPH Asia's role in opening new directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to non-standard contribution types
rubrics_metrics.description: Be open to types of contributions that do not fit the most common patterns of SIGGRAPH Asia papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes systems papers (novel integration of techniques), experimental studies (perceptual studies, material measurements), novel datasets and benchmarks, analysis of existing techniques—evaluate based on likelihood to inspire follow-on work even if they don't follow traditional validation patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical soundness and substantial contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each accepted paper should be technically sound and make a substantial contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor flaws can be corrected and should not be a reason to reject; focus on substantive contribution and technical correctness rather than polish alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format compliance and willingness to review submitted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: By accepting a paper for review, you commit to review all materials submitted in the approved formats: PDF for documents; for videos, MP4 and PNG or JPG for images are strongly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unwilling to make this guarantee, recuse yourself. Make reasonable effort to review materials in non-approved formats but not under the same absolute obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind anonymity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: We use double-blind reviewing. Authors are expected to strictly adhere to the Anonymity Policy; reviewers should not deliberately try to discover the identity of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors were asked to hide names/affiliations and omit acknowledgments. If you identify or suspect identity, report breaches; do not use identity to influence review. Plagiarism detection and sorting-team checks may follow; contact Technical Papers admin if you have substantial originality concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of URLs and external resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors were asked to refrain from including URLs referring to websites that contain vital material; anonymized links with verifiable timestamps before deadline are allowed in special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may generally ignore URLs unless absolutely necessary for review; if requesting comparisons provide public links to code/data. Authors allowed to add a link to a fully anonymized code/data repository with a verifiable timestamp prior to the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting anonymity and policy violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are obligated to report any policy violations and any breach of anonymity in the paper or supplementary material that lead to author identification for a paper they are reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the Technical Papers admin or chair; if timing of discovery makes reporting impossible without unfair impact, use judgment but generally report concerns to the admin before submitting your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparisons to prior work — scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are expected to compare to relevant published peer-reviewed work, but this requirement should not impose undue burden on the authors and preclude publication of highly promising contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different types of contributions require different types of validation; weigh requests for comparisons against whether they will affect the evaluation. Do not require exhaustive comparisons that impose unreasonable effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental comparisons required only to publicly available code/data
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental comparisons can be required only to publicly available code/data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting comparisons, provide public links to the code/data for the work to compare to. If no such code/data exists, do not expect authors to implement it; limit the request to discussion unless it is a minor change to an implemented method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require implementation of unavailable methods
rubrics_metrics.description: If no code or data is publicly available, do not expect authors to implement it unless it is a minor change to an already implemented method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit requests to discussion when code/data are unavailable; avoid asking authors to reproduce or reimplement non-public prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid requesting comparisons to hypothetically preferable approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not request comparisons to non-trivial to implement, hypothetically possible approaches, or adaptations of algorithms solving related but distinct problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have an alternative approach in mind that you consider preferable, consider writing a follow-up paper rather than using it as a reason to reject the current submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource-appropriateness for required comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Required resources for a comparison should not exceed those of a typical lab or already demonstrated in the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that require unique industrial-scale resources, special measurement devices, or very high-end hardware are inappropriate unless the contribution already uses such resources; insisting on such resources harms inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of preprints and recent non-peer-reviewed work
rubrics_metrics.description: Not everything available online is prior work. Existence of non-peer-reviewed materials (arXiv, reports) should not negatively affect your review, and authors are allowed but not required to cite them as concurrent work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preprints are not cited, authors of conditionally accepted papers can be asked to cite them in final revision. Do not expect detailed comparisons to very recent publications (e.g., published up to 4 weeks before the deadline); SIGGRAPH 2026 papers are not considered prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific and thorough in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Please be specific and detailed in your reviews; simply saying 'this is well known' or 'common practice' is not sufficient nor acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific publications or public disclosures of techniques, and if these do not exist, entertain the possibility the contribution is novel. The explanation section is one of the most important parts of your review and often more important than the numeric score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review scoring overview (single scale for tracks)
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions (dual-track and journal) are reviewed using a single scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As the journal requirements are a superset of conference requirements, uniformly strong scores for a dual-track submission indicate it should be accepted as a Journal paper; use scores together with explanation to guide track decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of reviews and rebuttal process
rubrics_metrics.description: The deadline for completed reviews is 25 June 2026. Adhering to this deadline is extremely important because the author rebuttal process starts immediately after the review deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete reviews by the deadline so authors can see the complete set of reviews for rebuttal; delayed reviews harm the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect ideas and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: You have the responsibility to protect the confidentiality of the ideas represented in the papers you review. Do not show the paper to anyone else, including colleagues or students, unless you have asked them to help with your review following proper procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not show videos or other materials to non-reviewers. Do not use ideas from papers you review to develop new ones. See Technical Papers FAQ for how to include a colleague or student properly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest — recusal and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: If your review would create a possible conflict of interest, return the paper immediately and do not submit a review; if you discover a conflict after starting, recuse yourself as soon as you discover it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts include (but are not limited to): same institution as an author; direct involvement in the work (e.g., committee member); perceived institutional conflicts (e.g., different locations of same company); collaboration within past three years (papers/grants); MS/PhD advisor or advisee (lifetime conflict); unpublished work that would get scooped by the submission. If in doubt, notify the senior reviewer or papers admin.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM use prohibition in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Large language models (LLMs) are NOT allowed to be used for writing the reviews nor the meta-reviews/summaries at any step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can't ask an LLM to write content for you or share substantial content from the paper or your review with an LLM (e.g., to translate a review). You can use an LLM for background research or to check short phrases for clarity. Grammar checker software that may have used LLMs is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be serious and avoid sketchy reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the review process is one of the most valuable assets of SIGGRAPH Asia; casual or flippant reviews are not appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write solid, constructive reviews. If you are too busy or not competent for a paper, return it early so a suitable replacement can be found; do not overcommit and then submit poor-quality reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be professional and constructive in tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Belittling or sarcastic comments, or comments on authors' personalities, have no place in the reviewing process. Evaluate the work, not the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide respectful, carefully explained strengths and weaknesses and how you weigh them, so authors can learn and improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer anonymity permanently
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers are expected to maintain anonymity forever. It is never appropriate for reviewers to reveal themselves to the authors of an accepted paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revealing identity could be perceived as attempting to curry favor. Be careful when requesting citations to your own work as this may thwart anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of review artifacts after completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously the guidelines required destroying copies; now reviewers may keep notes, marked manuscripts, or implementations if necessary because of possible future resubmissions where reviewers' names may be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you keep materials, insulate the ideas you learned from the review from your own research and colleagues/students. Be aware your reviews may be perused by future SIGGRAPH Asia reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to ACM and Eurographics digital libraries for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Eurographics and ACM Digital Libraries are available for reviewer usage and are open access for SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 paper reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must log in to access full text; username/password will be provided via the electronic review system. Use these resources to find and cite relevant prior work.
